The OSINT intelligence platform
Enter one person, company or website. It queries dozens of open sources, pivots on everything it finds, and hands back a source-attributed graph and a verified due-diligence report.

What is OSINT?
Open-source intelligence
Everything you can learn about a target from public sources — no hacking, no private access. The facts are already out there, in the open.
The skill isn't access. It's finding, connecting and proving the pieces, and knowing which ones are really about your target.
DNS records, WHOIS & certificates
Company & sanctions registries
Social profiles & usernames
Breach indexes & archived pages
Code repos & search engines
The problem
The sources are scattered. The analyst is the glue.
Tool switching
Dozens of websites and CLIs, each with its own query format and output.
Manual stitching
Copy-pasting identifiers between tools, rebuilding the links by hand.
False positives
A shared name or reused username drags in the wrong person's data.
No provenance
By the end, nobody can say which source a given fact actually came from.
What it does
One target in. A correlated, source-attributed graph out — built automatically and recursively.
PERSON
Name, email, username, phone
jane.doe@example.com
COMPANY
Legal name, reg. number, VAT
Example SRL · RO12345678
WEBSITE
Domain, URL or IP address
example.com · 203.0.113.10
A target is only a starting point. Every finding becomes a pivot: a website reveals an email, the email reveals a username, the username reveals social profiles — and the platform follows each lead for you.
The vocabulary
Four ideas run the whole system
01
Entity
A typed node: Person, Domain, IP, Email, Username, Organization, Certificate…
02
Connector
A plugin that queries one source. Declares the types it accepts and produces.
03
Finding
The raw result, stored unchanged with a timestamp and hash. Every fact traces back here.
04
Pivot
Running connectors on a newly found entity. Depth limits stop it running away.

Every lookup takes the same eight steps
Four ways to run it
From a cheap sweep to a full multi-agent dig
1
Quick scan — deterministic, no LLM. Fast, cheap, always available.
2
Collection agent — Claude chooses what to query and pivot on.
3
Report agent — reasons over the graph, cites and captures evidence.
4
Deep analysis — an orchestrator dispatches specialised workers in parallel.

How far to trust a source
Not every source is equal — so confidence is a number
confidence = 1 − Π (1 − reliability × match)
Each corroborating source multiplies in — independent sources agreeing push confidence up.
reliability per source type
0.95 official registry · DNS
0.90 certificate-transparency logs
0.70 commercial aggregators
0.60 scraped social profiles
0.40 username-match heuristics
Match quality matters too
An exact key scores 1.0; a name-only person match ≈ 0.3. A great source on a weak match is still weak.
The analyst is final
Confirming sets confidence to 1.0; rejecting hides the fact and teaches the resolver.
Conflicts are kept
Disagreeing values are all stored with their own sources; the UI shows the strongest and flags the clash.
From raw graph to a report you can send
AI verifies before a human reads a word
STEP 1
Verify
Claude rules on every entity: is this really the subject? A shared name is never enough — it needs a second matching detail, and can read pages or use research personas to check.
STEP 2
Write once
One writer, one dossier of everything that survived — so the report reads like a single author, not ten. Each claim cites the finding behind it.
STEP 3
Fact-check
A separate Claude checks every claim against its cited source. It flags the wrong person, overstatements and gaps; the writer fixes them in one round.
Only what the AI can't settle is left for the analyst — a short "needs you" list, not 249 raw rows.
Legal, ethics & safety
Built passive-first, with the brakes wired in
Passive by default
Anything that touches a target is active mode — gated, authorized, off by default.
Never invent a finding
Every claim traces to a stored artifact. If a tool returned nothing, it says so.
GDPR-proportionate
Data kept to the purpose; special-category data flagged; retention limits enforced.
Full audit trail
Who ran what, when, and why — every lookup recorded by the ledger.
The stack
Small, boring, and it fits on one box
Backend
Python 3.12 · FastAPI · httpx · the Anthropic & MCP SDKs · Playwright for screenshots · SQLite in WAL mode
Frontend
React · Vite · a live graph canvas · Tailwind — served as static files straight from the API
Infra
One 2-vCPU / 4-GB VPS · Docker Compose · Caddy for HTTPS and auth · VPN egress for collection
